title: Deep learning PET/CT-based radiomics integrates clinical data: A feasibility study to distinguish between tuberculosis nodules and lung cancer

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Deep learning PET/CT-based radiomics integrates clinical data: A feasibility study to distinguish between tuberculosis nodules and lung cancer》：研究问题的原文依据。

【INTRODUCTION · tca14924-sec-0005-p5】The objective of this study was to evaluate the classification performance of radiomic features, whilst also incorporating image and clinical information as reference factors for the classification of TB nodules and LC. It is important to note that the primary focus of this study was not to differentiate between general tuberculosis and lung cancer, but to examine specific cases. The tuberculosis nodules included in this study were extreme cases, necessitating the use of 18F‐FDG PET/CT and pathological confirmation to eliminate the possibility of lung cancer. Currently, cancer classification surveys tend to focus on separate fields such as imaging, clinical biochemistry, and genetic analysis. The integration of multidomain information in tumor analysis and studies holds promising prospects. The significance of this study was to improve the accuracy of the distinction between TB nodules and LC by combining information from radiomic features, deep learning features, and clinical information. The workflow of this study is illustrated in Figure 1.

【Background · abstract-1-1】Radiomic diagnosis models generally consider only a single dimension of information, leading to limitations in their diagnostic accuracy and reliability. The integration of multiple dimensions of information into the deep learning model have the potential to improve its diagnostic capabilities. The purpose of study was to evaluate the performance of deep learning model in distinguishing tuberculosis (TB) nodules and lung cancer (LC) based on deep learning features, radiomic features, and clinical information.

【Design of DCNN models · tca14924-sec-0011-p2】As shown in Figure 5, the deep learning feature extraction module is based on the ResNet architecture. A fully connected layer is utilized as a feature extractor, followed by an average pooling layer which serves as the connection to the classifier module. Subsequently, a dense layer of elements are connected and the sigmoid function is utilized to normalize the output value between 0 (representing 100% TB) and 1 (representing 100% LC). The input to the model consists of segmented PET and CT image patches. The model trains using the training set and is evaluated using the test set. If the assessment of the model improves from the previous iteration, the updated model is saved.

【Design of DCNN models · tca14924-sec-0011-p3】The integrated model was implemented using the Keras library (https://keras.io/). As shown in Figure 5, the integrated model integrates radiomic features, clinical information, and deep learning features to construct a unified system. The model consists of three separate modules, each of which processes image data, radiology data, and clinical data, respectively. A total of 1024 features are extracted by these modules. Additionally, the model has a feature selection function, which will be discussed in the discussion section. To summarize, the three sets of features are not simply summed but are processed through feature selection and extraction. It is noteworthy that after the integration of these three sets of features, no additional complex structures are employed. The goal is to make full use of the feedforward algorithm of the neural network, and to facilitate efficient feedback information flow to the feature extraction modules.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Deep learning PET/CT-based radiomics integrates clinical data: A feasibility study to distinguish between tuberculosis nodules and lung cancer》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【RESULTS · tca14924-sec-0013-p1】The study employed the bilinear interpolation method to resize the PET/CT image data to 50 × 50 voxels. The final image size of 50 × 50 × 100 was obtained by concatenating the PET and CT images along the channel dimension. The model's optimizer was set to Adam with a learning rate of 0.0001 and a decay of 0.01 for each training cycle. The loss function used was “binary cross entropy” and the evaluation metric used for each training epoch was the accuracy (ACC). The training process was run for a total of 100 epochs.

【RESULTS · tca14924-sec-0013-p2】As shown in Table 2, the classification performance of traditional radiomic classification (traditional radiomics) and DCNN relying on deep learning feature signals and convolutional neural network (radiomics‐DCNN) relying on radiomic signals and deep learning features signals and deep learning of the integrated radiomic signals convolutional neural network (integrated model) relying on radiomic signals, deep learning features signals and clinical information were evaluated. The AUC value of the integrated model was 0.84 (0.82–0.88), which was better than other models.

evidence.text: The study employed the bilinear interpolation method to resize the PET/CT image data to 50 × 50 voxels. The final image size of 50 × 50 × 100 was obtained by concatenating the PET and CT images along the channel dimension. The model's optimizer was set to Adam with a learning rate of 0.0001 and a decay of 0.01 for each training cycle. The loss function used was “binary cross entropy” and the evaluation metric used for each training epoch was the accuracy (ACC). The training process was run for a total of 100 epochs.

As shown in Table 2, the classification performance of traditional radiomic classification (traditional radiomics) and DCNN relying on deep learning feature signals and convolutional neural network (radiomics‐DCNN) relying on radiomic signals and deep learning features signals and deep learning of the integrated radiomic signals convolutional neural network (integrated model) relying on radiomic signals, deep learning features signals and clinical information were evaluated. The AUC value of the integrated model was 0.84 (0.82–0.88), which was better than other models.
